findings.title: Remove-and-re-add workaround has no documented home
findings.problem: The spec Decision (user, AR-4) chose documenting remove-and-re-add for members who joined a broken project before the fix over a backfill. No backfill was added, which is correct, but the workaround appears only in the spec's Non-goals; nothing in the diff, a guide or another repo doc carries it, and the spec does not say where it should live.
findings.impact: Members added to an already-broken project before this fix keep no budget allocation. Without a findable note, admins and support have no recorded way to repair them, so the user-chosen mitigation for skipping the backfill is effectively absent.
findings.recommendation: Decide where the workaround is documented (MR description, ticket, or a repo guide) and add it there: members who joined a broken project before the fix must be removed and re-added to get a budget allocation.
findings.check_notes: decision in fix_evidence: document remove-and-re-add in the MR description (Follow-ups / known limitations); rationale given

fix.change: No code change: remove-and-re-add workaround goes in the MR description under Follow-ups / known limitations (user decision)

decision.outcome: Document the remove-and-re-add workaround in the MR description only, under Reviewer notes -> Follow-ups / known limitations; no repo file changes.
decision.rationale: The MR template has a Follow-ups / known limitations line for deliberately-not-done work (.gitlab/merge_request_templates/Default.md:22); no budget guide exists, error-handling.md covers exception handling, and the spec non-goals rule out editing the provisioning guide.

findings.title: Duck-typed equal_share annotated as Any
findings.problem: code-quality.md Types And Imports requires spelling out the accepted union for a duck-typed parameter. shared_project_budget_amounts takes equal_share: Any | None, while callers pass a ProjectMemberBudgetAssignment, an EqualMemberShare or None. No Ruff rule in pyproject covers this.
findings.impact: Any switches off type checking for the one input that decides the shared row's amounts, so a caller passing an object without allocated_soft_budget/allocated_max_budget fails only at runtime. It breaks a documented project standard that the standards audit marks blocking.
findings.recommendation: Annotate equal_share as ProjectMemberBudgetAssignment | EqualMemberShare | None, or as a Protocol carrying allocated_soft_budget and allocated_max_budget.
findings.check_notes: budget_models.py:70 equal_share is ProjectMemberBudgetAssignment | EqualMemberShare | None; module has __future__ annotations

fix.change: shared_project_budget_amounts annotates equal_share as ProjectMemberBudgetAssignment | EqualMemberShare | None

findings.title: Shared row amounts not owned by row builder
findings.problem: Spec Behaviour 1 requires one pure function in budget_models.py that returns the whole shared row, amounts included, used by every creator. build_shared_project_budget_row takes soft_budget/max_budget from the caller and the amount rule is a separate shared_project_budget_amounts. Nothing forces a creator through the rule: _ensure_shared_child_budget_after_resync (project_budget_service.py:1239-1246) passes per-member sample amounts straight in. Acceptance graded the requirement partial.
findings.impact: Each creator still decides the shared row's amounts, so the single owner the spec chose over sharing only the field set is not achieved, and creators can diverge on the row's soft/max (e.g. the unenforced max) without a test noticing.
findings.recommendation: Decide: either fold the amount rule into build_shared_project_budget_row (take equal_share and enforce_limit instead of soft/max, and check whether routing _ensure_shared_child_budget_after_resync through it changes its results), or record that the two-function split satisfies Behaviour 1.
findings.check_notes: decision in fix_evidence: keep two-function split; resync now routes shared_sample through shared_project_budget_amounts (project_budget_service.py:1290-1295)

fix.change: Two-function split kept (user decision B); _resync_member_allocations now passes its shared sample through shared_project_budget_amounts, so every shared-row creator applies the one amount rule

decision.outcome: Option B: keep the two-function split. The shared row's amounts come from the separate pure function shared_project_budget_amounts in budget_models.py, which every creator calls; the resync creator now applies it where the resync sample is formed (project_budget_service._resync_member_allocations), keeping the (max, soft) order. Recorded in the MR description under Deviations from the ticket/spec.
decision.rationale: AC6's unchanged budget tests carry the task's no-regression requirement (Jira AC5) and pin _ensure_shared_child_budget's per_member_* kwargs; the single-function shape came from the architecture review, not the task or a requester decision. B removes the resync bypass so every creator applies the one amount rule with the smallest change.

findings.title: New code uses typing.Optional annotations
findings.problem: code-quality.md Types And Imports says to avoid typing.Optional[X] and use X | None. The new _first_equal_allocation returns Optional[ProjectMemberBudgetAssignment] (:112) and the new _ensure_shared_budget_row takes actor_id: Optional[str] (:147). The Ruff config selects no UP rules, so no gate catches it.
findings.impact: New code breaks a documented typing standard that the automated gate does not enforce; the standards audit marks code-quality partial, which blocks the review.
findings.recommendation: Annotate them as ProjectMemberBudgetAssignment | None and str | None.
findings.check_notes: _first_equal_allocation and _ensure_shared_budget_row removed; relocated helpers in shared_project_budget.py use X | None

fix.change: Optional annotations removed with the move: first_equal_member_allocation returns ProjectMemberBudgetAssignment | None, ensure_shared_project_budget_row takes actor_id: str | None

findings.title: Shared budget row creation in 780-line assignment module
findings.problem: code-quality.md Module Cohesion says not to add a concern that is not the file's core responsibility to a file of about 500 lines or more, and to extract first. _ensure_shared_budget_row (shared child Budget row creation with its own amount lookup, flush and logging, :146-181) was added to the 780-line membership assignment service.
findings.impact: Ownership of budget-row creation is split between the budget modules and the membership service, against the documented extract-first rule; the standards audit marks it blocking.
findings.recommendation: Move the shared-row creation into a budget-owned module (e.g. next to build_shared_project_budget_row) and call it from _sync_project_budget_member_added, keeping it in the caller's session and flushed before the allocation add.
findings.check_notes: shared-row creation moved to budget-owned shared_project_budget.py; assignment service calls ensure_shared_project_budget_row before the allocation add

fix.change: Shared-row creation and its equal-allocation lookup moved to new src/codemie/service/budget/shared_project_budget.py; the member-add sync calls it in the caller's session and flushes before the allocation add

findings.title: Admin grant-project-access lacks fixed member-add 500
findings.problem: POST /v1/admin/users/{user_id}/projects (user_management_router.py:336-349 -> UserAccessService.grant_project_access -> _apply_membership_change, user_access_service.py:185-194) runs the same project_assignment_service.assign_user_to_project member add, which now also inserts the shared row, then session.commit(), with no SQLAlchemyError mapping. Reactivation (user_management_service.py:488-491) re-runs the member-added sync the same way. Only the three membership.py routes use _member_assignment_errors, and no test covers a DB failure on these paths.
findings.impact: A DB failure while adding a member through these admin paths reaches the client as an unstructured 500 instead of the fixed 'nothing was saved' message the projects routes now return. AC3 says admin assign routes answer the fixed message, but Behaviour 3 enumerates only the three membership routes, so whether these paths are in scope needs a decision.
findings.recommendation: Decide whether AC3 covers grant-project-access (and reactivate). If yes, move _member_assignment_errors to a shared module, wrap the service call and commit in _apply_membership_change (user_access_service.py:185-194) and the reactivate route, and add a test asserting code 500, the fixed message and __cause__ for a flush failure and a commit failure.
findings.check_notes: decision in fix_evidence: grant-project-access and reactivation out of B3 scope, recorded in MR description; rationale given

fix.change: No code change: grant_project_access and reactivation keep the unstructured 500; scope recorded in the MR description under Deviations (user decision)

decision.outcome: No: grant_project_access (POST /v1/admin/users/{user_id}/projects) and user reactivation keep today's unstructured 500; the scope is recorded in the MR description under Deviations from the ticket/spec.
decision.rationale: The requester's Q1 answer and spec Behaviour 3 name exactly three routes (single, bulk, CSV import); the FK root cause is fixed for the admin paths anyway, and the fixed 'member could not be assigned' message would be wrong for reactivation.
